reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs with no comment, which is exactly what is expected for a compliant finding retained as internal evidence.

The cited text supports the rationale: Sections 9.1/9.2 impose only mutual record-keeping and retention duties with no access or examination right, and Section 3.6.1/3.6.2 give each Party (or PB) audit rights over its own third parties/facilities with report-sharing, not an SFJ audit right over PB. Section 3.18.2 is financial reporting plus executive meetings, not an audit right.

No frequency, notice, cost-allocation or systems-access exposure exists, and nothing falls in the walk-away zone; the absence of any audit right binding our party is better than the playbook's preferred position, so no redline is warranted (and flagging would be over-flagging a clause that benefits us).
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is explained by the absence of any Customer-facing audit clause rather than a defective edit, so it does not undermine the finding.

Rationale appropriately records the fallback negotiating position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost absent >5% discrepancy, no systems access) to be used if SFJ later seeks to add an audit right.
